'''Alberte Pullman''' (née '''Bucher''', 26 August 1920<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Alberte Pullman|url=http://www.iaqms.org/deceased/pullmana.php|publisher=iaqms.org|accessdate=11 October 2013}}</ref>  – 7 January 2011) was a French [[theoretical chemistry|theoretical]] and [[Quantum chemistry|quantum chemist]]. She is remembered for her early investigations into the electronic properties of carcinogenic [[aromatic hydrocarbon]]s, which she later developed with her husband [[Bernard Pullman]].

In early 2026, Pullman was confirmed to be one of the 72 women to have their names added to those of [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|the men already engraved on the Eiffel Tower]].

== Early life and education ==
Alberte Bucher was born on 26 August 1920 in [[Nantes, France]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=matchID - Moteur de recherche des décès |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/PtVOGWQJ-6wA |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=deces.matchid.io}}</ref> She studied at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] starting in 1938. During her studies she worked on calculations at [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS). From 1943 she worked with [[Raymond Daudel]], who had been [[Marie Curie]]'s assistant.<ref name=":1">[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-08</ref> She completed her doctorate in 1946,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stadler |first=Marta Macho |date=2025-11-25 |title=La 'revolución bioquímica' de Alberte Pullman |url=https://mujeresconciencia.com/2025/11/25/la-revolucion-bioquimica-de-alberte-pullman/ |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=Mujeres con ciencia |language=es}}</ref> with a 1946 thesis titled "The relation between the electronic structure and the carcinogenic properties of aromatic hydrocarbons" ({{Langx|fr|Contribution à l’étude de la structure électronique des molécules organiques. Etude particulière des Hydrocarbures cancérigènes}}).<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Bucher was in Paris during World War II and worked on theoretical chemistry, applying her findings to the study of biomolecules and pharmacology, particularly the carcinogenic properties of aromatic compounds.<ref name=":1" />

Alberte Bucher married fellow scientist [[Bernard Pullman]] following his return from war service in 1946, and took his surname. Her findings in the early 1940s strongly influenced his work. She and her husband worked together until his death in 1996. Together they wrote several books including ''Quantum Biochemistry'', Interscience Publishers, 1963. Their work in the 1950s and 1960s was the beginning of the new field of quantum biochemistry. They pioneered the application of [[quantum chemistry]] to predicting the [[carcinogenic]] properties of [[aromatic hydrocarbons]].<ref name=":0" />

She and her husband took an early interest in problems with cancer, both attending the meeting of the [[International Union Against Cancer]] in October 1953 in London.<ref name=fg/>

In this connection, together with her husband, she was an active participant in the series of [[Sanibel Symposium|Sanibel Symposia]] held in Florida. They also both attended the Jerusalem Symposia on Quantum Chemistry and Biochemistry, which Bernard Pullman had inaugurated in 1967,<ref name=fg/> and the Symposia at the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]. Together they are recognized for creating the field of quantum biochemistry.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zerner |first1=Michael C. |last2= |first2= |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/toc/1097461x/1999/75/3 |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry|volume=75 |issue=3 |publisher=Wiley|title=
Biophysics Quarterly: In Memory of Bernard Pullman |pages=137–138|issn=0020-7608|date=21 September 1999 |doi= |access-date=6 July 2026}}</ref>

In 1968, at the International Symposium on Atomic, Molecular, and Solid-State Theory, also known as the Sanibel Symposium, Alberte Pullman presented recent developments in [[quantum chemistry|quantum biochemistry]]. A pioneer in what was then a new field of research, she stressed the importance of [[intermolecular force]]s in connection with the recognition process, explaining how and whether molecules could fit together. She reported on the results she had obtained on pairings of [[Nucleotide base|nitrogen bases]] in the [[DNA molecule]] in living cells as opposed to those in crystallized materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1724343|title=Physics, Atomic, Molecular, and Solid-State|author=Edelson, Irc|publisher=Science, Vol. 160, No.3829|date=17 May 1968}}</ref>

Alberte Pullman also developed the supermolecule technique in connection with [[hydrogen bonding]], molecular hydration and cation binding. Her theoretical studies included examination of  the [[Ion transporter|transfer of ions]] through biological membranes.<ref name=":0" />

She was a member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] and a member of [https://isqbp.org/ The International Society of Quantum Biology and Pharmacology] which she headed from 1979 to 1980.<ref>[http://www.iaqms.org/members.php Members of IAQMS]</ref><ref name=fg/>

Pullman was Honorary Director of the Theoretical Biochemistry Department, [[Institut de biologie physico-chimique|Institut de Biologie Physico-Chimique]], and Directeur de Recherche Emerite at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]].<ref name=":0" />

Pullman died aged 90 on 7 January 2011 in the [[14th arrondissement of Paris|14e arrondissement of Paris]].<ref name=":2" />

== Honours and awards ==
Pullman was nominated four times for the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Burke |first=Maria |title=Nobel nominations analysis reveals factors behind who won in the past |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/nobel-nominations-analysis-reveals-factors-behind-who-won-in-the-past/4017517.article |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=Chemistry World |language=en}}</ref>

In 1956, together with her husband, she was awarded the Prix Essec du Cancer (Cancer Essec Award) with congratulations from the CNRS director Gilles Dupouy.<ref name=fg>{{cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/dossiers/fonds_pdf/Fonds_PullmanBernard.pdf|title=Fonds Bernard Pullman|publisher=Institut de France: Académie des Sciences|author=Greffe, Florence|year=2003|access-date=6 July 2026}}</ref>

In 1968, she received from the [[French Academy of Sciences]] the CEA prize (Prix du Commisariat à l'Énergie atomique) for dedicating her career to applications of theoretical chemistry to biology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/title/829#|title=Trois grands prix des sciences|publisher=Le Courrier de France|date=10 June 1988|page=12|access-date=6 July 2026|language=French}}</ref>

Pullman was made an officier of the [[Legion of Honour]] in 1989, and promoted to commandeur in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Décret du 14 mai 1994 portant promotion et nomination - Légifrance |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000000165202 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416021545/https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000000165202 |archive-date=2025-04-16 |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=www.legifrance.gouv.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

In 2026, Pullman was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names were proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was conceived by a student and tour guide named Bernard Rigaud<ref name="rigaud">{{Cite web |title=The Hypatia project: engraving the names of 72 women scientists on the Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en}}</ref> and it was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{citation |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref name="s72now">{{citation |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-06-16 |language=en}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Alberte Pullman authored some 350 publications, including three textbooks together with her husband and many reviews.<ref name=":0"/>

Published together with her husband in 1963, "Quantum Biochemistry" received critical praise from George Karreman in 1985 of the [[University of Chicago]]. Charles Perrin published a book review in 1964.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Perrin |first=Charles |date=November 1964 |title=Quantum Biochemistry (Pullman, Bernard; Pullman, Alberte) |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ed041pA888 |journal=Journal of Chemical Education |language=en |volume=41 |issue=11 |pages=A888 |doi=10.1021/ed041pA888 |issn=0021-9584|url-access=subscription }}</ref> After summarising the attention given to the [[Linear combination of atomic orbitals|Linear Combination of Atomic Orbital]] Molecular Orbital method in the first part of the book, he highlighted the hundred pages in the second part which present the results of these applications to the electronic structure of vitally significant biochemicals. The book's third part covers electronic aspects of [[enzyme catalysis|enzymatic reactions]], including the dipositive bond in [[enzymatic hydrolysis]]. With its extensive appendix of the results of quantum mechanical calculations of compounds of biochemical importance, the well-referenced book was recommended to all those interested in the new field it covers.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Karreman |first1=George |last2= |first2= |date= |title=Quantum Biochemistry |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/404410 |journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology |volume=35 |issue=4 |publisher=University of Chicago |pages=422 |doi= |access-date=6 July 2026}}</ref>

Alberte Pullman’s research was affiliated with the [https://ibpc.fr/ Institut de Biologie Physico-Chimique], [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] and other places. Researchgate records 164 publications by Alberte Pullman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alberte Pullman's research works {{!}} Institut de Biologie Physico-Chimique, French National Centre for Scientific Research, Paris (Ibpc) and other places |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Alberte-Pullman-60448603 |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=ResearchGate |language=en}}</ref>

* Transport Through Membranes: Carriers, Channels and Pumps: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Jerusalem Symposium on Quantum Chemistry and Biochemistry Held in Jerusalem, Israel, May 16–19, 1988.<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-94-009-3075-9 |title=Transport Through Membranes: Carriers, Channels and Pumps: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Jerusalem Symposium on Quantum Chemistry and Biochemistry Held in Jerusalem, Israel, May 16–19, 1988 |date=1988 |publisher=Springer Netherlands |isbn=978-94-010-7882-5 |editor-last=Pullman |editor-first=Alberte |series=The Jerusalem Symposia on Quantum Chemistry and Biochemistry |volume=21 |location=Dordrecht |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-94-009-3075-9 |editor-last2=Jortner |editor-first2=Joshua |editor-last3=Pullman |editor-first3=Bernard}}</ref>
* Model quantum-chemical studies on the reaction between the candidate proximate carcinogen benzo(a)pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-epoxide and guanine.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lavery |first=Richard |last2=Pullman |first2=Alberte |last3=Pullman |first3=Bernard |date=2009-06-18 |title=Model quantum-chemical studies on the reaction between the candidate proximate carcinogen benzo(a)pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-epoxide and guanine |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/qua.560140707 |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry |language=en |volume=14 |issue=S5 |pages=21–34 |doi=10.1002/qua.560140707|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* SCF ab initio study of the “through‐water” versus “direct” binding of the Na+ and Mg2+ cations to the phosphate anion.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pullman |first=Bernard |last2=Pullman |first2=Alberte |last3=Berthod |first3=Helene |date=2009-06-18 |title=SCF ab initio study of the “through-water” versus “direct” binding of the Na+ and Mg2+ cations to the phosphate anion |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/qua.560140711 |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry |language=en |volume=14 |issue=S5 |pages=79–90 |doi=10.1002/qua.560140711|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Electrostatic effect of the macromolecular structure on the biochemical reactivity of the nucleic acids. Significance for chemical carcinogenesis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pullman |first=Alberte |last2=Pullman |first2=Bernard |date=2009-06-19 |title=Electrostatic effect of the macromolecular structure on the biochemical reactivity of the nucleic acids. Significance for chemical carcinogenesis |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/qua.560180724 |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry |language=en |volume=18 |issue=S7 |pages=245–259 |doi=10.1002/qua.560180724|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Cation-Ionophore Interactions: Quantification of the Factors Underlying Selective Complexation by Means of Theoretical Computations.<ref>{{Citation |last=Gresh |first=Nohad |chapter=Cation-Ionophore Interactions: Quantification of the Factors Underlying Selective Complexation by Means of Theoretical Computations |date=2024-10-18 |title=Metal Ions in Biological Systems |pages=335–386 |chapter-url=https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/9781003573630/chapters/10.1201/9781003573630-12 |access-date=2026-07-10 |edition=1 |place=Boca Raton |publisher=CRC Press |language=en |doi=10.1201/9781003573630-12 |isbn=978-1-003-57363-0 |last2=Pullman |first2=Alberte|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>
